record.paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
record.context_brief: Microscopic derivation of IBM parameters far in the open shell
record.original_question: Can the parameters of the Interacting Boson Model be derived microscopically for nuclei far from closed shells, starting from the premise that s bosons and d bosons represent valence nucleon pairs in spherical orbitals coupled to spin 0 or spin 2?

evidence.quote: The collective quadrupole mode is described by means of the creation operators for nucleon pairs with spins 0 and 2, which are called s- and d- bosons and denoted by s† and d†, respectively, form the closed Lie algebra of the SU(6) group.

IBM assumes that the s and d bosons represent valence nucleon pairs in spherical orbitals that are coupled to spin 0 or 2. A microscopic derivation of the IBM parameters starting from this concept has not been succeeded for nuclei located far in the open shell.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Interacting Boson Model (IBM) describes low-lying collective quadrupole excitations of even–even atomic nuclei in terms of two kinds of bosons: an s-boson with angular momentum J=0 and a d-boson with angular momentum J=2, whose creation operators s† and (d†_μ)_{μ=-2,...,2} together with their adjoints and bilinears generate the Lie algebra of U(6). The standard IBM Hamiltonian is built from scalar combinations of these generators, e.g.

H_IBM = ε_d (d†·d̃) + κ Q·Q + κ' L·L + ...,

with a finite set of phenomenological parameters (such as ε_d, κ, κ', and the parameter χ in the quadrupole operator Q_μ = (s†d̃ + d†s)_μ + χ (d†d̃)_μ).

The physical premise of the model is that the s and d bosons represent collective valence-nucleon pairs in spherical single-particle orbitals coupled to total spin 0 and spin 2, respectively, on top of an inert closed-shell core. For nuclei with only a few valence nucleons (or holes) outside a closed shell, one can derive the IBM parameters microscopically from an underlying shell-model nucleon Hamiltonian by mapping collective fermion pair states onto boson states (e.g., via the OAI mapping or generalized seniority schemes).

Problem. Starting solely from the assumption that the s and d bosons represent valence-nucleon pairs in spherical orbitals coupled to angular momentum 0 and 2, give a microscopic derivation, from a realistic nucleonic Hamiltonian acting in the valence shell-model space, of the parameters of the IBM Hamiltonian (including ε_d, the strengths of the boson–boson interaction terms, and χ) that is valid for nuclei lying far from closed shells, i.e., near mid-shell where the number of valence pairs is large and deformed/transitional behaviour dominates. Equivalently, construct an explicit fermion-to-boson mapping procedure whose output IBM parameters reproduce, in a controlled approximation, the low-lying collective spectra and electromagnetic transition rates of mid-shell even–even nuclei.
artifact.category_tag: Interacting Boson Model / nuclear collective motion
artifact.status_search_result: Microscopic derivations of IBM parameters are well established for nuclei near closed shells (OAI mapping, generalized seniority, broken-pair approaches). For nuclei far in the open shell (mid-shell, strongly deformed), a fully microscopic derivation purely from the shell-model picture of valence pairs has not been achieved; modern approaches instead derive IBM parameters by mapping nuclear energy density functional / mean-field potential energy surfaces onto the IBM, providing a practical but indirect route. Thus the problem is partially solved: parameters can be obtained globally via mean-field mapping, but a direct microscopic derivation from the valence-pair shell-model premise for mid-shell nuclei remains an open issue.

status_evidence.title: Coexistence and evolution of shapes: mean-field-based interacting boson model
status_evidence.snippet: A modern method derives the IBM Hamiltonian based on the nuclear energy density functional framework, using self-consistent mean-field calculations... allowing determination of the IBM Hamiltonian for arbitrary nuclei from nucleonic degrees of freedom.
status_evidence.claim: Modern derivations of IBM parameters for arbitrary (including mid-shell) nuclei proceed via mean-field/EDF mapping rather than a direct shell-model valence-pair derivation.

status_evidence.title: Application of a microscopic interacting boson model to single-closed-shell nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: A microscopic interacting boson approximation is systematically formulated in spherical nuclei with matrix elements calculated from a nucleon Hamiltonian.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic derivations from a nucleon Hamiltonian are established mainly for single-closed-shell (near-closed-shell) nuclei.

status_evidence.title: New Microscopic Derivation of the Interacting Boson Model and Its Applications to Exotic Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: New microscopic derivation of the IBM and applications to exotic nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on improving the microscopic derivation of the IBM, indicating that the problem is not fully resolved.
